samples.summary: Overlay guard is broader than the problem it fixes: `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]` also matches an open Radix **Tooltip**, which is not dismissable-on-Esc and does not take focus. `SidebarMenuButton` renders a Tooltip/TooltipContent for every nav item (packages/frontend/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:534-543, used via nav-main.tsx:44) and Radix mounts the content — hence the popper wrapper — whenever the trigger is hovered/focused (the `hidden` prop only visually hides it when the sidebar is expanded). While such a tooltip is mounted the viewer silently drops BOTH Esc and ←/→. The task doc's last acceptance criterion is "Unchanged: pdf/file layouts, ←/→ prev/next, zoom, download, share" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-image-viewer-back-button-todo.md:22), so making arrow navigation conditional on no tooltip being mounted anywhere in the document deviates from it. A guard scoped to actually-dismissable layers (`[data-state="open"]` roles / `[aria-modal]`) would fix the reported ShareDialog/Sheet case without touching tooltips.

Design doc not updated for the behavior this delta adds. §"Leaving the viewer (issue #840)" still describes only "Esc obeys the same input/contenteditable guard as ←/→"; the new rule — the viewer ignores Esc and ←/→ whenever any open Radix overlay (dialog/menu/listbox/popper) is mounted, enforced from a window capture-phase listener specifically so it can observe the overlay before Radix unmounts it — is a user-visible keyboard contract nothing in docs/design or the active todo records (the todo, lines 35-36, still describes plain Escape handling in the existing keydown handler).

`hasOpenOverlay()` is the third ad-hoc Radix-overlay detector inside packages/frontend alone — `app/spreadsheet/components/comments/CommentPopover.tsx:58-62` checks `[role="menu"] / [role="dialog"] / [data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]`, and `app/slides/slides-image-input.ts:166-172` checks `[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal="true"]` for the same "an overlay owns this event" question. The repo expects reuse; one shared helper (e.g. under `src/lib/`) would keep the selector list in one place rather than three subtly different ones that drift as Radix markup changes. Judgement call, since the existing copies answer a pointer-target question rather than a global "is anything open" question.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as quoted: OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR includes "[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]" (image-viewer.tsx:22-30) and hasOpenOverlay() short-circuits the whole key handler before ArrowLeft/ArrowRight as well as Escape (image-viewer.tsx:139-153). The scenario is reachable on this route: FileShell always renders AppSidebar (file-shell.tsx:109-116), NavMain passes tooltip={item.title} for every nav item (nav-main.tsx:42-49), SidebarMenuButton wraps them in Tooltip/TooltipContent with only a `hidden` DOM prop (sidebar.tsx:534-544) — Radix still mounts the popper wrapper — and TooltipProvider uses delayDuration = 0 (tooltip.tsx:6-16), so a hover/focus on any sidebar nav item mounts the wrapper and silently disables ←/→ in the viewer. The task doc's acceptance criterion "Unchanged: pdf/file layouts, ←/→ prev/next, zoom, download, share" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-image-viewer-back-button-todo.md:22) and plan step 5 (only the input/contenteditable guard was specified, line 35-36) make this a spec-conformance/unrequested-scope issue in the design-fit lane, i.e. major kind. No guard elsewhere prevents it, so no named refutation ground applies.
